landing.title: OpenFarmPlanner
landing.heroImageAlt: Vegetable garden beds in front of a wooded mountainside
landing.subtitle: Open-source crop planning for vegetable production.
landing.description: Designed specifically for market gardens, community-supported agriculture, and other farms with many crops and small-scale growing areas.

demoPage.title: Try the demo
demoPage.subtitle: Test OpenFarmPlanner instantly with a temporary example project.
demoPage.description: This link can be shared directly. A demo workspace is created only when you actively start the demo.
demoPage.safetyNote: The demo does not require registration. Changes are deleted automatically and are not intended for real production data.

statusOpenSource.text: As an open-source project, we welcome feedback, ideas, and contributions.

productTour.title: Season planning at a glance
productTour.description: A realistic demo project shows how growing areas, crops, schedules, and summaries work together in practice.

areas.title: Edit areas and beds directly
areas.description: Locations, fields, and beds stay visible in a clear hierarchy. Changes happen right in the table – no separate forms or page switches.
areas.alt: Table view of growing areas with locations, fields, and beds

plantingPlans.title: Edit planting plans directly
plantingPlans.description: Sowing, planting, and harvest dates, as well as quantities and crops, can be edited right in the table. Changes show up immediately, making season planning fast.
plantingPlans.alt: Planting-plan table with crops, areas, dates, and planned quantities

calendar.title: Plan bed occupancy in the calendar
calendar.description: The cultivation calendar shows which crop occupies each bed and when, making overlaps easy to spot early.
calendar.alt: Cultivation calendar with occupied beds and colored crop periods

seedDemand.title: Derive seed demand from plans
seedDemand.description: Seed amount and package suggestions are calculated from crop parameters, used area, and supplier data.
seedDemand.alt: Seed demand table with crops, suppliers, required amount, and package suggestions

yieldOverview.title: Keep expected harvests in view
yieldOverview.description: The yield overview groups planned harvest quantities by period and crop, making peaks and distribution visible early.
yieldOverview.alt: Yield overview with expected harvest quantities by calendar week and crop

crops.title: Maintain crops centrally
crops.description: Varieties, cultivation methods, spacing, expected yield, and seed data live in one place and feed the plan.
crops.alt: Crops view with several vegetables and varieties in the demo project

generalNotice.title: General information
generalNotice.content:
We process your personal data confidentially and in accordance with the applicable data protection laws and this privacy policy. This privacy policy supplements the terms of service of OpenFarmPlanner. For questions about the processing of personal data, this privacy policy is exclusively authoritative.

You can use the OpenFarmPlanner landing page without providing any personal data. As soon as you create a user account and use the application, we process the data described in the following sections. For each processing activity, the legal basis stated there under Art. 6(1) GDPR is authoritative.

hosting.title: Hosting
hosting.content:
This application is hosted by the following provider, which acts as our processor:

Uberspace GmbH
Kaiserstraße 15
55116 Mainz
Germany

When the application is accessed, the web server processes technical access data:

bullets.ipAddress: shortened IP address (for IPv4 only the first 16 bits, for IPv6 only the first 32 bits are stored)
bullets.requestTime: Date and time of the request

hosting.legalBasis:
The web server log files are deleted automatically after 7 days. In addition, we process technical application logs (for example Django or Gunicorn error logs). These primarily contain technical information such as error messages, timestamps, and affected requests; in individual error cases relating to account, login, or invitation management, they may also contain the affected email address, username, or an internal user ID. The logs are used exclusively for troubleshooting and secure, stable operation of the application.

Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest in secure and stable operation of the application).

registration.title: Registration and user account
registration.content: To use OpenFarmPlanner, you can create a user account, either with an email address and password or alternatively via your Google account (see the "Sign-in with Google" section). When registering with an email address and password, the following data may be processed:

bullets.emailAddress: Email address (visible to other members of the same project in the member list; never published publicly)
bullets.encryptedPassword: Password (stored securely hashed – not viewable by us in plain text)

registration.legalBasis: Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (performance of a contract)

socialLogin.title: Sign-in with Google
socialLogin.content: In addition to registering with an email address and password, you can register and sign in to OpenFarmPlanner with your Google account (Google Sign-In). When you click "Sign in with Google", you are redirected to Google; after signing in successfully with Google, you are redirected back to OpenFarmPlanner.

bullets.receivedData: From Google, we receive your email address, your first and last name, a stable Google account identifier, and, if transmitted by Google, a profile picture URL and your language setting stored with Google.
bullets.storedData: Only your email address and first name are copied into your OpenFarmPlanner account. We additionally store Google's full login response (including the Google account identifier, profile picture URL, and language setting, where transmitted) in a separate technical record used for login management, so that we can recognize you on future Google sign-ins.
bullets.purpose: This data is used exclusively for account creation and sign-in. OpenFarmPlanner does not call any Google APIs after sign-in and does not store any Google access tokens.
bullets.disconnect: You can disconnect your Google account at any time in the account settings under "Sign-in methods", provided you have another way to sign in (a password or another connected provider).

socialLogin.legalBasis: Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (performance of a contract by providing an alternative sign-in method). For the transfer to Google, see the "Third-country transfers" section.

projectData.title: Project and application data
projectData.content: Within your projects, we process the project-related data entered by you and other project members. This includes, in particular, master data of the project (e.g. project name, memberships and locations), operational planning and management data for the features in use (e.g. relating to fields, crops, cultivation planning or tasks), and supplementary information such as notes, uploaded files, and the change history, including the display name of the person who made the change. This data is generally visible only to you and the other members of the respective project.

publicLibrary.title: Public crop library
publicLibrary.content: You can publish individual crop records (for example growing information about a vegetable variety) from a private project into a public crop library yourself. This library is intended as a collaboratively built, permanently maintained knowledge base. Published entries can be viewed by other users, imported into their own projects, and in future reused through features such as version histories, collaborative editing, comments, ratings, public APIs or data exports. Publishing is voluntary and is not required in order to use OpenFarmPlanner. Which rights of use you grant to the general public and to OpenFarmPlanner by doing so is governed by the terms of service, in particular the section "Open licence for published crop data".

bullets.publicContent: Only the agricultural growing data of the crop is published (for example name, variety, growth and harvest duration, plant spacing, seed quantity). Notes from the private project, as well as project-internal information such as seed suppliers, are not published.
bullets.attribution: The author of a published entry is shown using the public display name that you can choose freely in your account settings. This name belongs to your account, not to the individual entry: if you set it for the first time or change it, it automatically appears as the author on all crops you have already published; if you remove it again, those entries are shown anonymously once more. Previous names are not stored on individual entries. If you have not set a public display name, publication is anonymous, without any name. The display name must be unique; when it is set, a technical check verifies whether it is already used by another account. Your username and your email address are never part of a public entry; the email address is used solely for account management and for our communication with you (see the section "Email communication").
bullets.noReview: Publication happens immediately and directly through you; there is currently no review or approval of the content by us.
bullets.persistence: A published entry generally remains part of the public library permanently, even if you later change or delete the original crop in your private project.
bullets.removal: Removal is not provided as a normal user feature. It is only considered in exceptional cases, such as legal violations, personal data in the published record, spam, obvious abuse, or a moderation decision.
bullets.futureOutlook: In the long term the crop library is intended to be developed collaboratively. Feedback on entries should in future be given through features inside the application — such as comments, ratings, version histories, public APIs or data exports — and not through other users' personal contact details.

publicLibrary.legalBasis: Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR, insofar as we make your contribution available in the public crop library on the basis of the terms of service and your explicit act of publication. Insofar as published contributions still contain personal references, for example through the public display name, and we retain them permanently for the integrity and traceability of the collaborative knowledge base, we additionally rely on Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our legitimate interest lies in building and maintaining a reliable open crop database. Purely factual or anonymised crop data does not fall under the GDPR.

emailCommunication.title: Email communication
emailCommunication.content: We use your email address for:

bullets.systemNotifications: other communication related to your user account, such as system notifications

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.content: OpenFarmPlanner uses only technically necessary cookies. No analytics, tracking, or marketing cookies are used. The cookies are used only to enable logged-in use of the application and to protect requests technically. The specific storage period depends on the server's session and security configuration; session cookies are deleted at the latest when they expire or when you delete them in your browser.

bullets.sessionCookies: Session cookie to maintain your login (legal basis: Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR - without this cookie, logged-in use of the application cannot be provided)
bullets.securityCookies: Security cookie for protection against cross-site request forgery, or CSRF (legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR, legitimate interest in securing the application)

localStorage.title: Local storage (Local Storage/Session Storage)
localStorage.content: In addition to cookies, the application stores individual technical settings in your browser's local storage (Local Storage/Session Storage). This includes, in particular, the last opened project, view options, sidebar and table states, sorting and filters, hints that have already been shown, and temporarily stored redirects or tokens for project invitations. This data does not leave your device, is not visible to us, and does not contain login credentials. Local Storage data remains in your browser until it is replaced by the application, reset by you in the application, or deleted via browser functions; Session Storage data is usually deleted when the browser tab is closed. Because we do not process this data on our systems, this is not processing of personal data by us within the meaning of Art. 4 No. 2 GDPR; a separate legal basis is therefore not applicable.

dataSharing.title: Data sharing
dataSharing.content:
Apart from cooperation with our hosting provider as a processor (see the Hosting section), we share your personal data only if:

- this is necessary for technical email delivery in connection with your account or project invitations; email delivery uses the mail infrastructure operated by Uberspace,
- you sign in or register with your Google account; in that case, Google receives the technical data required for sign-in (see the "Sign-in with Google" and "Third-country transfers" sections),
- you actively publish a crop in the public crop library and thereby choose visibility for all logged-in users, including your public display name if you have set one (see the Public crop library section), or
- we are legally required to do so, for example toward authorities.

thirdCountryTransfers.title: Third-country transfers
thirdCountryTransfers.content:
If you sign in or register with your Google account (see the "Sign-in with Google" section), personal data is transferred to Google LLC, headquartered in the USA. To the best of our current knowledge, Google LLC is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (DPF). The European Commission has determined that an adequate level of data protection applies to data transferred to certified companies (adequacy decision under Art. 45 GDPR of July 10, 2023). You can check the current certification status yourself at any time via the official DPF participant list (https://www.dataprivacyframework.gov/list).

Beyond that, based on the current assessment, personal data is not transferred to recipients outside the European Union or the European Economic Area. Sign-in with a Microsoft account is prepared in the OpenFarmPlanner source code but not currently activated; it will only become part of this privacy policy once activated.

mandatoryProvision.title: Provision of personal data
mandatoryProvision.content: Providing personal data is neither legally nor contractually required if you only visit the public landing page. For registration and use of the application, your email address, password, and technically necessary cookies are required; without this data we cannot provide a user account or enable login. You provide project and application data voluntarily when you want to use the relevant features; without this information, the corresponding planning features cannot be used or can be used only in a limited way. Publishing to the public crop library is voluntary and is not required for using the rest of the application.

storageDuration.title: Storage duration
storageDuration.content:
Your account data is stored as long as your user account exists. User accounts that are not activated are deleted after the activation period expires; activation links are currently valid for 7 days. Password reset links are currently valid for 3 days; email change links are currently valid for 24 hours. Project invitations are currently valid for 14 days; after that period, the invitation record still exists but can no longer be accepted. If you use the unauthenticated demo feature ("Try demo"), the data created during that session is automatically deleted no later than 8 hours after the session started.

If you request account deletion, the account is first marked for deletion for 14 days; during this period, you can undo the deletion. After that period, we anonymize your account (email address and display name are removed, the account is deactivated, and a connected Google sign-in is removed) and remove your project memberships, unless legal obligations or other compelling reasons prevent this.

Projects remain as long as at least one member exists. If a project has no members after account deletion, we delete the project including its project-specific data. Published entries in the public crop library are not affected and remain part of the public knowledge base (see the Project and application data and Public crop library sections). Server log files of the hosting provider are deleted after 7 days; IP addresses are stored in shortened form by Uberspace. We automatically delete our own scheduled-maintenance (cron job) logs no later than 14 days after they are created. Our application's own error output (Django/Gunicorn) is not stored in log files we manage ourselves; it is captured by our hosting provider's process management, whose own technical configuration determines how long it is retained. There are currently no further statutory retention obligations for the data we process because OpenFarmPlanner does not process billing- or tax-relevant data.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.content: As a data subject, you have the following rights under the GDPR:

bullets.access: Access to the data stored about you (Art. 15 GDPR)
bullets.objection: Objection to processing based on legitimate interest (Art. 21 GDPR)
bullets.consentWithdrawal: Withdrawal of a consent you have given, with effect for the future, without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out until then (Art. 7(3) GDPR)

rights.contact: You can correct your account data, export your data, and request account deletion directly in the account settings. For exceptional cases that are not covered by these self-service functions, the controller remains reachable at info@openfarmplanner.org.

complaint.title: Right to lodge a complaint
complaint.content:
In addition to the rights listed above, you have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority if you believe that the processing of your personal data infringes the GDPR (Art. 77 GDPR). In particular, you may contact the supervisory authority of your habitual residence, your place of work, or the place of the alleged infringement.

For OpenFarmPlanner, the Austrian Data Protection Authority is the competent supervisory authority in Austria:

Austrian Data Protection Authority
Barichgasse 40-42
1030 Vienna
https://www.dsb.gv.at

changes.title: Changes to this privacy policy
changes.content: We update this privacy policy when the processing of personal data changes due to new features or changed legal requirements. The version published in the application applies. The date of the last change is shown at the end of this privacy policy. We inform active users about material changes in an appropriate way, for example by email or through a notice within the application.

scope.title: Scope and use of the platform
scope.content:
These Terms of Service apply to the use of OpenFarmPlanner, a web application for planning agricultural and horticultural cultivation. By registering a user account or using the application, you accept these Terms of Service.

OpenFarmPlanner is intended for private individuals as well as agricultural and horticultural businesses that want to organize their cultivation planning digitally. Information on the processing of personal data can be found in the Privacy Policy.

serviceAndCosts.title: Service scope
serviceAndCosts.content: OpenFarmPlanner provides digital planning functions as a hosted web application.

accounts.title: User accounts
accounts.content:
A user account is required to use the application. You are obliged to provide truthful information during registration and to keep your password confidential.

You are responsible for all activities carried out through your user account. Please inform us immediately at info@openfarmplanner.org if you suspect that someone has gained unauthorized access to your account. A user account is personal and non-transferable.

userContent.title: Your content in OpenFarmPlanner
userContent.content:
Within your projects, you can create your own data, such as location, field and crop data, cultivation plans, tasks, notes, and photos. You are responsible for the accuracy, completeness, and legality of this content.

Do not upload content for which you do not have the necessary rights, such as copyrighted photos of third parties.

publicLibrary.title: Public crop library
publicLibrary.content:
You can voluntarily publish individual crop records from a private project into the public crop library. This library is intended as a collaboratively built, permanently maintained knowledge base for agricultural and horticultural crop data. Published entries are visible to other users, can be imported into their own projects, and may in the long term be reused through features such as version histories, collaborative editing, comments, ratings, public APIs, or data exports.

By publishing, you confirm that the published information is accurate to the best of your knowledge, contains no personal data of third parties, and that you are entitled to publish it permanently under the open license named in these terms of service.

contributionLicense.title: Open license for published crop data
contributionLicense.content:
When you publish a crop record to the public crop library, you license the published crop data under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International license (CC BY-SA 4.0). This license in particular allows third parties to reproduce, distribute, edit, and combine the published crop data with other data, and to use it commercially, provided the license terms are followed. These terms include, in particular, appropriate attribution, an indication of the license, and sharing modified versions under the same or compatible terms.

Once validly granted, the license is irrevocable under its terms. OpenFarmPlanner may permanently store and display the published crop data, include it in search and import features, make it available in public data exports or APIs, technically process it, and further develop it as part of the collaborative crop library.

prohibitedContent.title: Prohibited content and behavior
prohibitedContent.content: When using OpenFarmPlanner, especially when publishing content in the public crop library, it is not permitted to

bullets.illegalContent: post unlawful, misleading, or third-party-rights-infringing content (for example copyright or personality rights),
bullets.malware: distribute malware or bypass security measures of the application,
bullets.abuse: misuse the application in an automated way, for example through mass registrations or spam,
bullets.misrepresentation: impersonate another person or knowingly publish false information.

copyright.title: Copyright
copyright.content:
The OpenFarmPlanner software is protected by copyright and is licensed under the license named in the "Open-source software" section. The content you enter, such as crop data or notes, remains your property.

If you believe that an entry published in the public crop library infringes your copyright or other rights, please contact info@openfarmplanner.org. We investigate justified notices (see the "Content removal" section).

contentRemoval.title: Content removal
contentRemoval.content:
Published entries in the crop library are generally intended to remain permanently and are not removed as a normal user feature on request. However, we reserve the right to remove, block, or anonymize published content in whole or in part, or to correct it in the future through moderation or versioning features, where there are concrete indications of a violation of these terms of service or applicable law. This applies in particular to legal violations, personal data in the published record, spam, obvious abuse, misleading information, or a moderation decision.

You can report suspected unlawful or problematic content at any time to info@openfarmplanner.org. We are not obliged to carry out general, proactive monitoring of published content.

accountSuspension.title: Suspension of user accounts
accountSuspension.content:
In the event of a serious or repeated violation of these Terms of Service, we may temporarily restrict access to your user account or suspend the account. We proceed proportionately and take into account the severity of the violation and whether it is an isolated or repeated incident.

In the event of suspension, we will inform you of the reason where possible. You can contact info@openfarmplanner.org at any time about this.

liability.title: Liability
liability.content:
OpenFarmPlanner is developed and operated with great care. Nevertheless, we cannot guarantee error-free or uninterrupted availability at all times, for example during maintenance, technical disruptions, or events outside our control.

The public crop library contains content created by users themselves. The respective publishing users are responsible for its accuracy, not OpenFarmPlanner (see the "Your content in OpenFarmPlanner" section).

Agricultural and horticultural information in OpenFarmPlanner, such as growth and harvest periods, plant spacing, or seed quantities, is intended only to support your own cultivation planning and does not replace professional advice.

For damages resulting from slightly negligent breaches of duty, our liability is limited. Our liability for intent and gross negligence as well as for damages resulting from injury to life, body, or health remains unaffected, as do other mandatory statutory liability rules.

openSource.title: Open-source software
openSource.content:
The OpenFarmPlanner source code is published as open-source software under the GNU Affero General Public License Version 3 (AGPLv3) and can be viewed, reused, and modified in the OpenFarmPlanner GitHub repository (https://github.com/OpenFarmPlanner/planner). The license regulates only the rights to the software itself and, as is common with open-source software, excludes any warranty for the software.

This is separate from use of the hosted application at openfarmplanner.org, which is governed by these Terms of Service.

futureFeatures.title: Further development of the platform
futureFeatures.content: OpenFarmPlanner is continuously developed. These Terms of Service apply analogously to future features around user-provided content, such as comments, ratings, or version histories for entries in the public crop library. In the case of material new functions of this kind, we will update these Terms of Service if necessary (see the "Changes to these Terms of Service" section).

changes.title: Changes to these Terms of Service
changes.content: We update these Terms of Service if the offered functions or legal framework change. The version published within the application at the time of your use is authoritative; the date of the last change can be found at the top of this page. In the event of material changes, we will inform active users in an appropriate way, for example by email or through a notice in the application.

languageVersions.title: Language versions
languageVersions.content: This document is provided in German and English. In the event of any discrepancy or ambiguity between the language versions, the English version shall prevail.
